Error metrics show downlink BLER was very low, between 0 and 0.0036 (mean 0.00099), whereas uplink BLER was higher, between 0.052 and 0.17 with a mean of 0.1, indicating more uplink retransmissions. Uplink PRB allocation and utilization were generally light: PRBs_UL_Current spanned 0 to 5.5 (mean 0.7) and PRB_Utilization_UL ranged 0 to 5.2 (mean 0.68). Downlink PRB occupancy and utilization experienced multiple sharp events—PRBs_DL_Current ranged 0 to 64 with a mean of 14.2, and PRB_Utilization_DL ranged 0.095 to 61 with a mean of 13.8; notable spikes reached the upper end of the scale. 

Traffic and buffer behaviour were bursty. TX_Bytes showed at least seven significant jumps and drops (overall range 0 to 390,000 Bytes, mean 69,872.5 Bytes) including a major fall from ~373,808 to ~16,822 Bytes. RX_Bytes ranged from 46.0 to 22,726.0 Bytes with a mean of 2,070.9 Bytes. The estimated uplink buffer varied from 14.0 KB to 2,019.6 KB and averaged 191.3 KB, consistent with intermittent uplink queuing. Packet counts reflected the same burstiness: UL_NumberOfPackets ranged 0 to 81 (mean 17.5) and DL_NumberOfPackets ranged 0 to 280 (mean 59.1).

Finally, transport-layer usage was overwhelmingly TCP: DL_Protocol was TCP for 98.44% of samples and UL_Protocol was TCP for 99.22% of samples.

- **Resolution:** Reduced source/receiver mobility, reoriented antennas for optimal alignment, and updated scheduling/adaptation algorithms to improve performance under mobility scenarios.
